pages.subtitle: An early bishop who wrote seven letters on his way to Rome, and the first to call the Church "catholic."

quick_facts.label: From
quick_facts.value: Antioch, in Syria, where he was bishop

quick_facts.label: Known for
quick_facts.value: His seven letters and his great love for Jesus and the Church

pages.intro: Ignatius was one of the very first bishops of the Church. He led the Christians of Antioch, the city where followers of Jesus were first called Christians. When he was arrested for his faith, he was taken all the way to Rome. On the journey, he wrote seven letters full of love for Jesus. We can still read them today.
story_paragraphs: Ignatius lived in the time right after the apostles. He was the bishop of Antioch, a great city in Syria. Antioch was special. The Bible says it was there that the followers of Jesus were first called Christians.
Ignatius called himself Theophorus. That name means "God-bearer," someone who carries God inside him.
Around the year 107, Ignatius was arrested because he was a Christian. Roman soldiers led him on a long journey from Antioch to Rome, where he was to be put to death.
Along the way, the soldiers stopped in different cities. Christians came out to meet their bishop and to pray with him. In the city of Smyrna, he was welcomed by its bishop, Saint Polycarp.

On the journey, Ignatius wrote seven letters. Six went to churches in different cities, and one went to his friend Polycarp. In them, he begged Christians to stay united, to love one another, and to stay close to their bishop. He called the Eucharist "the medicine of immortality."

In one letter, Ignatius wrote, "Wherever Jesus Christ is, there is the Catholic Church." He is the first Christian writer we know of to use the word "catholic." It means "universal," or "for everyone everywhere."

Ignatius was not afraid to die. He wrote to the Christians in Rome and asked them not to try to save him. He wanted to give his whole life to Jesus. He said he was like wheat, ready to become bread for Christ.
In Rome, Ignatius was put to death in the great arena. He gave his life for Jesus, just as he had hoped. His letters have been treasured by Christians for more than 1,900 years.

pages.subtitle: A bishop who learned from Saint John the Apostle and stayed faithful to Jesus for 86 years.

quick_facts.label: From
quick_facts.value: Smyrna, in what is now Turkey

quick_facts.label: Known for
quick_facts.value: Learning from Saint John and staying faithful to Jesus his whole life

pages.intro: Polycarp grew up in a Christian family not long after Jesus lived. He learned about Jesus from Saint John, one of the twelve apostles. He became the bishop of Smyrna and cared for his people for many years. When he was an old man, he was told to give up his faith. He answered that Jesus had always been good to him.
story_paragraphs: Polycarp was born around the year 69, into a family that already believed in Jesus. As a young man, he became a disciple of Saint John the Apostle, the friend of Jesus who wrote one of the Gospels. Imagine learning about Jesus from someone who had walked with him!
Polycarp became the bishop of Smyrna, a busy city by the sea in what is now Turkey. He led the Christians there for many years.

In the year 107, a bishop named Ignatius came through Smyrna as a prisoner on his way to Rome. Polycarp welcomed him. Later, Polycarp gathered the letters Ignatius had written and sent them to other Christians so they could learn from them.
Polycarp wrote a letter of his own to the Christians of Philippi. He told them to serve God, to hope in the resurrection, and to live good and fair lives.

When he was very old, Polycarp traveled all the way to Rome to meet Pope Anicetus. Christians in the East and in Rome celebrated Easter on different days. The two leaders talked it over. They did not agree, but they stayed friends.

Then a time of persecution came to Smyrna. Polycarp was arrested. The Roman official told him to curse Christ and save himself. Polycarp answered, "I have served Him for eighty-six years, and he has done me no harm." He would not turn away from Jesus.

Polycarp was put to death in the year 155. An old account, written by people who were there, says that when the soldiers lit a fire around him, the flames did not touch him. In the end, he gave his life for Jesus.
That account is one of the oldest stories of a martyr that we have.

pages.subtitle: A thinker who searched everywhere for the truth, found it in Jesus, and taught it for free.

quick_facts.label: From
quick_facts.value: Flavia Neapolis, in Samaria, in the Holy Land

quick_facts.label: Known for
quick_facts.value: Searching for truth and explaining the faith to others

pages.intro: Justin loved to ask big questions. Where does the world come from? What is true? He studied with many teachers, but none of their answers satisfied him. Then an old man told him about the prophets and about Jesus. Justin became a Christian and opened a school to teach about Jesus. He wrote the oldest description of the Mass that we have.
story_paragraphs: Justin was born around the year 100 in Samaria, in the Holy Land. His family did not believe in the one true God. They worshiped many false gods.

Justin was very curious. He wanted to know what was really true. He went to different teachers called philosophers, people who think deeply about life and the world. He studied with one teacher, then another, then another. Each one taught him something, but none of them gave him the answers he was looking for.

One day, Justin went off alone to think. Near the seashore, he met a mysterious old man. They talked for a long time. The old man told Justin that people cannot find God by their own thinking alone. He told him to read the prophets of the Bible, who spoke about Jesus.
Justin read the Scriptures, and his heart was set on fire. He became a Christian and was baptized. He said that the Christian faith was "the only sure and profitable philosophy."

Justin moved to Rome and opened a school. He taught about Jesus for free to anyone who wanted to learn. He also wrote books to defend Christians, who were being treated unfairly. In one of them, he described what Christians did when they gathered for the Eucharist. It is the oldest description of the Mass that we have.
Justin believed that everything good and true in the world comes from God. He wrote, "Everything beautiful, no matter who said it, belongs to us Christians."

Around the year 165, a man who disliked Christians had Justin arrested. Justin and six other Christians refused to give up their faith. They were put to death together in Rome. That is why he is called Justin Martyr.

pages.subtitle: Two young mothers in North Africa, one rich and one a slave, who stood together as sisters in Christ.

quick_facts.label: From
quick_facts.value: Carthage, in North Africa

quick_facts.label: Known for
quick_facts.value: Their courage and the prison diary Perpetua wrote

pages.intro: Perpetua was a young mother from a well-off family. Felicity was a slave who worked in her household. In the eyes of the world they were very different, but in Christ they were sisters. In the year 203, they were arrested together for being Christians. In prison, Perpetua wrote down what happened. Her diary is one of the oldest writings by a woman that we have.
story_paragraphs: Long ago, in the city of Carthage in North Africa, lived a young woman named Perpetua. She came from a family with money. She was married and had a baby son, only a few months old. Her servant, Felicity, was a slave. Felicity was going to have a baby too.

Perpetua and Felicity were preparing to be baptized. At that time, the Roman emperor had made a law against becoming a Christian. In the year 203, they were arrested together with three young men who were also learning about the faith. Their teacher, Saturus, chose to join them in prison.

Perpetua's father was not a Christian. He came to the prison and begged her to give up her faith. He even brought her baby to her. Perpetua loved her father and her son very much. But she answered simply, "I am a Christian."

In prison, Perpetua kept a diary. She wrote down what happened and also the dreams God gave her. In one dream, she saw a golden ladder that reached up to heaven. A serpent lay at the bottom, but she was not afraid. She said it would not hurt her, "because Jesus Christ is in me."
While they were in prison, Felicity's baby was born. Christians in the city took care of the little one.
On March 7, 203, Perpetua, Felicity, and their friends were put to death in the arena. They went bravely and calmly, like people already on their way to heaven.
Today, Perpetua and Felicity are remembered together. A rich woman and a slave woman, they show us that in God's family, everyone is equal.

pages.subtitle: A deacon of Rome who showed an emperor the real treasure of the Church: the poor.

quick_facts.label: From
quick_facts.value: Spain, according to tradition

quick_facts.label: Known for
quick_facts.value: Caring for the poor and calling them the treasures of the Church

pages.intro: Lawrence was a deacon in Rome. His job was to care for the Church's money and to help orphans, widows, and people who were poor. When the emperor demanded the treasures of the Church, Lawrence brought him the poor and the sick. These, he said, were the Church's real treasures. Lawrence gave his life for Jesus in the year 258.
story_paragraphs: Lawrence was born in Spain in the 200s. He came to Rome, where he served the Church as a deacon. Deacons help the bishop, and in Rome there were seven of them.

When Sixtus II became pope, he trusted Lawrence with a very important job. Lawrence took care of the Church's goods and used them to help people in need. He looked after orphans, widows, and families who were poor. He knew them by name.
In the year 258, the Roman emperor Valerian made a cruel law. All bishops, priests, and deacons were to be put to death. Pope Sixtus was arrested and was killed on August 6.
Lawrence was arrested too. The emperor's officials believed the Church had hidden riches. They told Lawrence they would spare his life if he handed over "the treasures of the Church."

Lawrence asked for a little time. Then he gathered the people he served: the sick, the hungry, the poor, and people no one else cared about. He brought them before the officials. "These are the treasures of the Church," he said.

The officials were furious. Four days after the Pope died, on August 10, Lawrence was put to death. He stayed faithful and brave until the end. He had given his life to serving the poor, and now he gave it to Jesus.
The emperor Constantine later built a church over Lawrence's tomb in Rome. Christians have honored him ever since.
In August, when Lawrence's feast comes around, shooting stars often streak across the night sky. An old folk tradition calls them the tears of Saint Lawrence.

pages.subtitle: A girl of about twelve who gave her whole heart to Jesus.

quick_facts.label: From
quick_facts.value: Rome

quick_facts.label: Known for
quick_facts.value: Her brave faith as a young girl, and the lamb that is her symbol

pages.intro: Agnes was a young girl in Rome, only about twelve or thirteen years old. She loved Jesus with her whole heart. During a time when Christians were persecuted, she would not turn away from him, even when grown-ups pressured her. Agnes became one of the best-loved saints of Rome. Every year on her feast day, two lambs are blessed in her honor.
story_paragraphs: Agnes lived in Rome long ago, at a time when it was against the law to be a Christian. Many Christians were arrested and put to death for their faith.

We do not know many facts about Agnes's life. We know that she was very young, only about twelve or thirteen years old, and that she gave her life for Jesus. We know she was buried near Rome, and that Christians began to honor her very soon after she died.

Old stories tell us more. They say Agnes was beautiful and that many young men wanted to marry her. But Agnes had already given her heart to Jesus, and she said no to all of them. One of the young men was angry. He told the officials that Agnes was a Christian.

Agnes was arrested. The officials tried to frighten her into giving up her faith. But this young girl was braver than the grown-ups around her. She would not turn away from Jesus. In the end, she was put to death.

Agnes's name sounds like the Latin word "agnus," which means "lamb." The lamb has become her symbol. An old story says that after she died, her parents saw her in a vision, holding a pure white lamb in her arms.
The daughter of the emperor Constantine built a church in her honor in Rome. Agnes is buried there today.
Every year on January 21, two lambs are brought to the Pope and blessed at the church of Saint Agnes. Their wool is later used to make the pallium, a special white band worn by archbishops.

pages.subtitle: A young woman of Rome who "sang in her heart to the Lord" and became the patron saint of music.

quick_facts.label: From
quick_facts.value: Rome

quick_facts.label: Known for
quick_facts.value: Her faith, her courage, and being the patron saint of music

pages.intro: Cecilia was a young woman from a noble family in Rome. She gave her life to Jesus, and the old stories say she led her husband and his brother to the faith too. She is the patron saint of music and musicians. Her feast day prayer says that she "sang in her heart only to the Lord." Many choirs and music schools are named for her.
story_paragraphs: Cecilia lived in Rome about 1,800 years ago. Tradition says she came from a noble family. She died as a martyr, probably around the year 230.

Much of what we know about Cecilia comes from an old story written long after she died. The Church says this story is more like a legend than history. But it has inspired Christians for hundreds of years.

The story says Cecilia had promised her life to God. Her parents arranged for her to marry a young man named Valerian. On their wedding day, Cecilia told Valerian that she loved Jesus with her whole heart. Valerian was moved. He was baptized, and so was his brother, Tiburtius. Later, both brothers were put to death for being Christians.
Then Cecilia was arrested. The story says she stayed brave and kept her faith. Before she died, she gave all she had to the poor and gave her house to the Church.

Today, a church stands in Rome where her house is said to have been. In the year 1600, workers there found her body. It was in a surprisingly good state. An artist named Stefano Maderno carved a statue of her lying just as she was found. The statue is still in the church.

Why is Cecilia the patron saint of music? The prayer for her feast day says that while the instruments played, "she sang in her heart only to the Lord." Artists began to paint her with an organ and other instruments. Today, singers and musicians all over the world ask for her prayers.

pages.intro: Lucy lived on the island of Sicily long ago. She came from a wealthy family, but she chose to give her riches to people who were poor. During a time of persecution, she would not give up her faith in Jesus. Her name is linked with light, and her feast falls in December, when the days are darkest. Many people celebrate her with candles.
story_paragraphs: Lucy was born near the end of the 200s in Syracuse, a city on the island of Sicily. Her family was wealthy and important. Her father had died, and she lived with her mother, Eutychia.
Most of what we know about Lucy comes from old stories, passed down and written long after she lived. They tell us a lot about her faith.

The stories say Lucy's mother was very sick. Doctors could not help her. In the year 301, Lucy and her mother traveled to the city of Catania to pray at the tomb of another saint, Agatha. There, Lucy had a vision. Saint Agatha told her that her own faith had helped her mother, and that her mother was already healed.
Lucy was thankful. She asked her mother if she could sell the money and goods saved up for her wedding and give them to the poor. Her mother agreed.
But the young man Lucy was supposed to marry was angry. He reported Lucy to the governor as a Christian. At that time, the emperor Diocletian had made a law against Christians.
Lucy was arrested and told to worship false gods. She refused. On December 13, 304, Lucy was put to death for her faith.

Lucy's name is linked with light, and she is honored as a patron of sight. Her feast comes in December, close to the longest night of the year. In Sweden and other countries, girls dress in white and wear crowns of candles on Saint Lucy's Day.

pages.subtitle: A brave young woman of Sicily whose people still ask for her prayers when the volcano rumbles.

pages.intro: Agatha was a young Christian woman who lived on the island of Sicily long ago. During a time of persecution, she would not give up her faith in Jesus, and she gave her life for him in the city of Catania. The people of Catania have loved her ever since. When the nearby volcano, Mount Etna, erupts, they ask for her prayers.
story_paragraphs: Agatha lived on the island of Sicily, in the south of Italy, about 1,800 years ago. She was a young woman who loved Jesus.
In the year 250, the Roman emperor Decius ordered everyone in the empire to worship the Roman gods. Christians who refused could be arrested. Many Christians in Sicily were.

Almost nothing about Agatha's life is known for certain. What we do know is that she was arrested for being a Christian and that she would not turn away from Jesus. She died as a martyr in Catania, a city in Sicily, around the year 251.

Old stories say more. They say Agatha had given her life to God and that a powerful man wanted her to give up her faith. She was put in prison and treated very cruelly. Vatican News says that, through it all, she "proved a brave fidelity to Christ." That means she stayed faithful to Jesus, no matter what.

After Agatha died, the people of Catania began to ask for her prayers. Catania sits near Mount Etna, a very large volcano. About a year after Agatha died, Etna erupted. The people prayed to God through Agatha's help, and the eruption stopped. They believed her prayers had protected them.
Ever since, the people of Sicily have asked Agatha to pray for them, especially for protection from fire. Both Catania and Palermo, two cities of Sicily, call her their patron saint.
Agatha was so loved that another young woman, Saint Lucy, later traveled to her tomb to pray.

pages.intro: Sebastian was a Christian in Rome who gave his life for Jesus long ago. Old stories say he was an officer in the Roman army who secretly helped Christians in prison. When the emperor found out, Sebastian was sentenced to be shot with arrows. He is a patron saint of athletes, and his church in Rome is visited by pilgrims from all over the world.
story_paragraphs: Sebastian lived in Rome near the end of the 200s, when the emperor Diocletian ruled. It was a dangerous time to be a Christian.

We know for sure that Sebastian was a martyr in Rome. Christians were already honoring him by the year 350, and Saint Ambrose, a great bishop, wrote about him. He was buried in a Christian burial place under the ground, called a catacomb, on the edge of Rome.

The rest of his story comes from old legends. They say Sebastian joined the Roman army and became an officer. Because he was a soldier, no one suspected him of being a Christian. That let him visit Christians in prison and give them courage.

One day his secret was discovered. He was brought before the emperor, who sentenced him to be shot with arrows. The legend says that when friends came to bury him, they found him still alive. They took care of him until he was well again.
Sebastian could have run away to safety, but he did not. He went back and told the emperor bravely that it was wrong to treat Christians so cruelly. This time, the emperor had him put to death.
A church was later built over Sebastian's burial place. Today it is one of seven great churches that pilgrims in Rome visit. An arrow said to be from his martyrdom is kept there.
Because Sebastian was strong and brave, he is a patron saint of athletes and soldiers. Artists have painted him for hundreds of years.

pages.subtitle: A soldier who would not give up his faith, and the hero of a famous legend about a dragon.

quick_facts.label: From

pages.intro: George was a Christian soldier who gave his life for Jesus around the year 303. He is one of the most famous saints in the world. He is the patron saint of England and of many other places. Most people know him from a famous legend in which he defeats a dragon. The real George was brave in a different way: he would not deny Jesus.
story_paragraphs: George was born around the year 280 in Cappadocia, in what is now Turkey. His family was Christian. His name comes from a Greek word that means "farmer." Later he moved to Palestine, in the Holy Land.

George became a soldier in the army of the emperor Diocletian. In the year 303, Diocletian made a cruel law against Christians. George would not obey it. He gave away what he owned to the poor. Then, the story says, he tore up the emperor's order right in front of the emperor. He said out loud that he was a Christian.
For this, George was arrested and put to death. He was buried at Lydda, a town in the Holy Land now called Lod. A church was built over his grave.
We do not know much more about George's life for certain. In 1969, the Church noted that many facts about him are missing. But Christians have loved him for more than 1,600 years.

Later, people told a famous legend about George. In it, a dragon lived in a pond near a town in Libya. The people had to feed it sheep. One day the king's daughter was chosen to be given to the dragon. George rode up on his horse, struck the dragon with his spear, and saved her. Then the king and his people promised to be baptized.
The dragon is not a real animal, but the story has a real lesson. It shows good defeating evil with God's help.
George became the patron saint of England, and of knights, soldiers, and scouts.

pages.subtitle: A bishop remembered for saving a boy who was choking, and for the blessing of throats each February.

quick_facts.label: From
quick_facts.value: Sebaste, in Armenia, where he was bishop

quick_facts.label: Known for
quick_facts.value: The blessing of throats on his feast day

pages.intro: Blaise was a bishop in Armenia who gave his life for Jesus around the year 316. An old story says he once saved a boy who was choking on a fish bone. That is why, on his feast day, February 3, many Catholics go to church to have their throats blessed. The priest holds two crossed candles against each person's throat and prays for them.
story_paragraphs: Blaise lived about 1,700 years ago. He was the bishop of Sebaste, a city in Armenia. He cared for his people's souls and also for their health.
In the year 311, the Roman Empire made a law that allowed Christians to worship freely. But in Armenia, Christians were still being persecuted.
Most of what we know about Blaise comes from a story written about 400 years after he lived. It is a legend, but it has inspired Christians for many centuries.

The legend says Blaise had to flee from his city. He lived alone as a hermit in the wild countryside. There he made friends with the wild animals. One day, hunters came looking for animals. They found Blaise kneeling in prayer, with wolves, lions, and bears all around him, and none of them hurt him.

The hunters arrested Blaise. On the way to prison, a worried mother ran up to him. Her young son had a fish bone stuck in his throat and could not breathe. Blaise prayed over the boy, and the boy coughed up the bone. He was saved!
The governor told Blaise to worship false gods. Blaise refused, and he was put to death around the year 316.

Because of the story of the boy, Catholics ask Blaise to pray for them when they have throat sicknesses. Every year on February 3, priests bless people's throats. They hold two candles, crossed like an X, against each person's throat and pray, "Through the intercession of Saint Blaise, bishop and martyr, may God deliver you from every disease of the throat and from every other illness."
